A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiveResearchBench and DeepEval work. Their text, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v4 reports original evaluations of 17 research systems, citation-error measurements, human–judge alignment studies, and user-survey findings.

after.justification: v5 retains original system evaluations and survey findings and additionally reports human validation of citation-accuracy judgments.

M1.justification: The DeepEval protocols, Gemini 2.5 Pro/GPT-5 ensemble, rubric-tree citation checker, and Deerflow+ controls are retained. Citation Traceability renames Citation Association without changing its substantive instructions or scoring rubric.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 100-task benchmark across seven domains. Citation-accuracy evaluation retains market analysis and wide information search. The additional human validation does not introduce new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix B.2 newly includes Claude-4-Opus among judges tested for direct-scoring variability. The 17-system comparison and three-system citation-accuracy comparison retain their membership. The additional benchmarks in Table 6 are literature comparisons, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v5 adds a human-validation protocol using 200 randomly sampled claim–URL–judge-decision records in Appendix C. Existing generation settings, scoring rubrics, judge ensemble, and pairwise comparison rules are retained; the PDFs do not establish that the benchmark evaluations were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C extends judge-reliability analysis to Citation Accuracy, absent from v4's alignment appendix. v5 also reports additional diagnostics of direct-scoring instability. Existing citation-error analyses, Deerflow case studies, and presentation breakdowns are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B.2 newly report independent judging runs and differences exceeding 50 points in holistic depth ratings. This adds variability reporting, but no run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or evidence of increased repetitions.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises citation scores for all 17 systems: GPT-4.1 changes from 66.9 to 50.6 and Grok-4 Heavy from 64.7 to 48.0. Gemini Deep Research overtakes Grok-4 Deep Research within their category. Average-result entries are removed; the other three columns and relocated citation-error counts remain unchanged. New findings include 87.1% citation-accuracy human agreement and the reported judging variability. The score revisions are unexplained.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical definitions are added or revised. Existing scoring rubrics and depth-score aggregation rules are retained.

C1.justification: Both retain the central contributions: a 100-task benchmark, six-dimensional DeepEval, evaluation of 17 systems, and findings of weak citation reliability and analytical depth. Abstract and contribution-bullet edits do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 adds explanations that separating presentation prevents stylistic issues being conflated with factual errors, and that depth and global-consistency assessment discourage shallow but well-cited responses. Existing memory, compression, and coverage–depth interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v5 removes the statement that full-dataset release awaits institutional approval, without confirming release. Appendix B.2 explicitly documents web-search APIs for judging. The code-access link and Deerflow+ implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix B and Table 6 substantially expand positioning through a six-criterion comparison of ten prior benchmarks and detailed evaluation-protocol discussions. ScholarSearch, BrowseComp, and ReportBench citations are added. Section 2 also qualifies its earlier broad characterization of prior benchmarks' limitations.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized rewrites and cuts, renames the citation metric and judge-ensemble heading, adds acknowledgments and conference headers, and organizes expanded related work and relocated citation analysis into appendices. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds comparison Table 6, removes Table 1's Average column and shortens its caption, and relocates v4 Figure 5 and Table 2 to appendix Figure 13 and Table 7. Other figures move, and Figure 22's rendering changes while its plotted values remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revised Table 1 resolves an internal inconsistency: v4's multi-agent citation scores average 69.3 although its prose states 61.9; v5's entries now yield 61.9. Added citation-accuracy human validation and expanded research positioning provide further useful support. These gains are limited by unexplained score revisions and new cross-benchmark agreement comparisons without established matching protocols.
